rationale: C05 plausibly supplied a material template for the child’s central organizational proposal. Both directives organize foreign-assistance operations as a single unit within the Department of State, place it under one senior administrator reporting directly to the Secretary, preserve a distinct Defense role for military assistance, and emphasize unified administration without dispersing operating responsibility. The child adapts this machinery by replacing the International Cooperation Administration and Development Loan Fund with AID. C25 and C07 contain closely related coordination and chief-of-mission machinery, but C05 most directly anticipates the child’s agency structure and reporting arrangement.

shared_material.child_excerpt: Responsibility and authority for the formulation and execution of the foreign development aid programs will be assigned to a single agency--the Agency for International Development--within the Department of State.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: related Mutual Security operations should be brought together in a single organization under a single management. Consistent with this approach we should avoid dispersal of operating responsibilities either within the Department or to agencies outside the Department.
shared_material.explanation: The child reuses the parent’s central single-agency, unified-management design while substituting AID for ICA.

shared_material.child_excerpt: The new agency--AID--will be headed by an Administrator of Under Secretary rank reporting directly to the Secretary of State and the President.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: A new semi-autonomous organizational unit, to be known as the International Cooperation Administration, will be established in the Department of State... The Director of the International Cooperation Administration will report directly to the Secretary of State.
shared_material.explanation: Both establish a distinct foreign-assistance unit inside State headed by a senior official with a direct reporting line to the Secretary.

shared_material.child_excerpt: The principal assignments of authority for the administration of military assistance are satisfactory and will remain unchanged. The Department of Defense has operational responsibility for approved programs... the Secretary of State provides continuous supervision and general direction of the program.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: the Secretary of State will be responsible for coordinating all Mutual Security programs, which will of course include the establishment of arrangements with the Secretary of Defense for effectively coordinating Mutual Security programs involving the Department of Defense.
shared_material.explanation: Both preserve Defense’s role while placing overarching coordination or supervision with the Secretary of State.
